renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: recovered_community
  title: Community recovered by each binning run
  description: |-
    Each bar is a binning run, split into the taxa of one rank and sized by the number of bins placed in each. It answers which organisms each combination of assembler and binner recovered.
    How to read: switch the rank with the control. Two binners on the same assembly rarely recover the same set, and a binner with many more taxa than its neighbour is either more sensitive or splitting one genome into pieces. The bin quality tiles say which.
    Note: the eight largest taxa are drawn and the rest are grouped as Other.
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    default_rank: phylum
    normalise_to_one: false
    top_n: 8
    x_title: Binning run
    value_title: Bins
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    taxon: taxon
    rank: rank
    abundance: abundance

- component: figure
  title: Bins per taxon and binning run
  description: |-
    Each bar is a binning run, stacked by taxon and sized by the number of bins. It answers how many bins each run recovered and from which taxa.
    How to read: taller bars are runs that recovered more bins, and a bar with many colours is a run that recovered diverse taxa. Pick a rank in the rank filter, since without one the bars add up the bins of every rank.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample_id
    y: abundance
    color: taxon
    labels:
      sample_id: Binning run
      abundance: Bins
      taxon: Taxon

- component: card
  title: Phyla recovered by binner
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct phyla recovered, and the bars rank the binners by their phyla. It answers how diverse the recovered community is and which binner found most.
    How to read: a binner far ahead of the others is more sensitive or splits genomes, so check the bin quality before preferring it.
  column: taxon
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: binner
  top_n_count: 5
  filter_expr: col('rank') == 'phylum'
  caption: the binners that recovered the most phyla, with the row count

- component: card
  title: Bins by assembler
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of bins placed at phylum rank over the rows in view, and the bar splits it by assembler. It answers which assembler produced most of the bins.
    How to read: a bin that stopped above phylum rank is not counted. An assembler with a small share recovered fewer genomes.
  column: abundance
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: assembler
  filter_expr: col('rank') == 'phylum'
  caption: split by assembler, with the median and largest count per phylum

- component: card
  title: Bins per phylum
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of bins per phylum in a run, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how many bins a typical phylum has.
    How to read: a median of one means most taxa are found as a single bin, and larger values mean several bins per taxon, which can be redundant bins of one genome.
  column: abundance
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('rank') == 'phylum'
  caption: median, with its spread across phyla

- component: interactive
  title: Rank filter
  description: Pick one taxonomic rank to keep. The bar chart adds the bins of every rank when no rank is
    picked, so choose one.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: rank

- component: table
  title: Recovered taxa table
  description: |-
    Each row is a binning run, a rank and a taxon, with the number of bins placed in it. It answers the exact counts behind the community views.
    How to read: filter on a rank and sort by bins to find the dominant taxa of a run.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: lineage_sunburst
  title: Taxonomic lineage of the bins
  description: |-
    Each arc is a taxon of the GTDB lineage, from domain in the centre outwards, sized by the number of bins placed in it and coloured by phylum. It answers which organisms the recovered bins belong to.
    How to read: a wide arc is a taxon with many bins. A bin that stops at a high rank was placed only that far, which can mean the database holds few related genomes. Use the rank control to move the inner ring and open the table for the bins.
  kind: sunburst
  config:
    colour_by_rank: phylum
  roles:
    ranks:
    - domain
    - phylum
    - class_name
    - order
    - family
    - genus
    abundance: bin_count

- component: advanced_viz
  id: assembler_binner_phylum
  title: Assembler, binner and phylum of the bins
  description: |-
    Each flow is a group of bins that goes from an assembler through a binner to a phylum, with the width of the flow equal to the number of bins. It answers which combinations of assembler and binner recover which phyla.
    How to read: a phylum reached from every binner is recovered robustly, and a phylum reached from one binner only is a candidate for being missed by the others. Thick flows into a node mark the combinations that recover the most bins.
  kind: sankey
  config:
    value_label: Bins
  roles:
    steps:
    - assembler
    - binner
    - phylum

- component: advanced_viz
  id: ani_vs_alignment
  title: Closest reference identity against alignment fraction
  description: |-
    Each point is a bin: its average nucleotide identity (ANI) to the closest GTDB species representative on the horizontal axis and the fraction of the genome aligned to it on the vertical axis, coloured by phylum. It answers how confidently a bin matches a known species.
    How to read: points to the upper right, with high identity and alignment, are assigned to a species. A point with a low alignment fraction or low identity is a novel lineage or a poor bin, and may stop at a higher rank. The ANI needed is specific to each species, typically 95 percent, so no vertical line is drawn.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the minimum alignment fraction of 0.5, the GTDB-Tk default (--min_af) for assigning a genome to a species during the ANI screen. The species-specific ANI radius is typically 95 percent.
    Source: https://ecogenomics.github.io/GTDBTk/faq.html and https://ecogenomics.github.io/GTDBTk/commands/classify.html
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Average nucleotide identity to the closest reference (%)
    y_title: Alignment fraction to the closest reference
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_value: 0.5
    reference_label: Minimum alignment fraction (0.5)
    top_n_labels: 5
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: closest_ani
    y: closest_af
    label: bin_id
    color: phylum

- component: figure
  title: Bins recovered per phylum
  description: |-
    Each bar is a phylum, sized by the number of bins placed in it and split by the binner that recovered them. It answers which phyla were recovered and by which binners.
    How to read: a phylum recovered by one binner only is a candidate for being missed by the others. A long tail of phyla with one bin each is typical of a diverse community.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: phylum
    y: bin_count
    color: binner
    labels:
      phylum: Phylum
      bin_count: Bins
      binner: Binner

- component: card
  title: Bins by phylum
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct bins classified, and the bars rank the phyla that hold the most. It answers how many bins were placed in the database and in which phyla.
    How to read: a single phylum holding most bins points to a low diversity community or to bins that are fragments of the same genomes.
  column: bin_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: phylum
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: the five phyla with the most bins, with the row count

- component: card
  title: Species by genus
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct species the bins were assigned to, and the bars rank the genera that hold the most. It answers how many species level identities the run recovered.
    How to read: the row count above the distinct count means several bins share a species, which is expected when binners or assemblers recover the same genome. Bins stopped at a higher rank have no species and are not counted.
  column: species
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: genus
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: the five genera with the most species, with the row count

- component: card
  title: Bins by deepest rank
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct bins, and the ring splits them by the deepest taxonomic rank GTDB-Tk reached. It answers how many bins are identified to species and how many stop earlier.
    How to read: a ring mostly at species means the community is well represented in the database. A large share at a higher rank marks novel lineages or bins of poor quality.
  column: bin_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: rank_assigned
  caption: split by the deepest rank reached, with the row count

- component: card
  title: Identity to the closest reference
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median ANI of a bin to its closest reference genome, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how close the recovered genomes are to known species.
    How to read: values near the top of the scale mean the bins are close to known species. Only bins classified by the ANI screen carry a value, so an empty card means the run was placed through the tree. The species specific radius is typically 95 percent.
    Source: https://ecogenomics.github.io/GTDBTk/faq.html
  column: closest_ani
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across bins

- component: card
  title: Alignment fraction to the closest reference
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean fraction of a bin aligned to its closest reference genome, and the histogram shows how the values are distributed. It answers how much of each bin is covered by a known genome.
    How to read: values near 1 mean the bin and the reference share nearly all their sequence, and low values mean only part of the bin matches. GTDB-Tk requires an alignment fraction of at least 0.5 for a species assignment by ANI.
    Source: https://ecogenomics.github.io/GTDBTk/commands/classify.html
  column: closest_af
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: average and median, with the smallest and the distribution

- component: table
  title: Bin taxonomy table
  description: |-
    Each row is a bin with its assembler, binner, lineage split by rank, closest reference, ANI, alignment fraction and classification method. It answers which organism each bin is and how it was placed.
    How to read: filter by phylum or by deepest rank, and sort by ANI to find the least certain species assignments.
